rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of me. I'm not able to give an on-the-record comment for this piece, so please don't quote or name me or Halcyon Threshold in it. Halcyon Threshold is a very early, small personal project and there isn't anything ready to talk about yet. I'd be glad to hear from you again in future. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Tessa Brandt (Larkin Dispatch) saying no on-the-record comment, and asked her not to name you or Halcyon Threshold.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, this is a really kind offer, and a data analyst is exactly what's useful right now. The project I'm looking into is a careful, sourced dataset of the public safety commitments frontier AI developers have made (pre-deployment testing, incident reporting, security, external researcher access, etc.) and the public evidence on whether each has been kept. Before building anything I want to check we wouldn't just be duplicating someone else. So a concrete first task, roughly 2 weeks at your pace: 1. Find existing trackers or datasets of AI lab commitments or follow-through (academic, NGO, journalistic, and hobbyist ones). 2. For each, note: who maintains it, scope, how often it's updated, whether the data is downloadable/licensed for reuse, and what it misses. 3. Give your gut call on whether there's a real gap, or whether we'd do more good by contributing to one of them. A simple spreadsheet is perfect. No pressure on timing. If this doesn't appeal, tell me and we'll find something else. All of this is private and low-key for now. I'm not putting the project out publicly yet. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman and gave her a first task: spend about two weeks finding existing trackers and judging whether there's a real gap.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly review" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Set up a weekly review every Monday at 9am (`sched_1`).
